mainEntity.name: How long does composite bonding last for grinding damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding typically lasts 3-7 years when properly maintained, though longevity depends on factors like grinding severity, oral hygiene, and protective measures used. Using a night guard significantly extends the lifespan of bonding repairs by preventing continued grinding damage.

mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding painful for worn tooth edges?

acceptedAnswer.text: The bonding procedure itself is generally comfortable, as it typically requires minimal tooth preparation. Local anaesthetic is rarely needed unless sensitivity is present. Some patients experience mild sensitivity immediately after treatment, but this usually resolves within a few days.

mainEntity.name: Can severe grinding damage be treated with bonding alone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mild to moderate grinding damage often responds well to composite bonding, but severe wear may require more comprehensive treatments like crowns or veneers. Your dentist will assess the extent of damage to determine the most appropriate restorative approach for your situation.

mainEntity.name: Will bonding change how my teeth feel when I bite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Initially, restored teeth may feel slightly different when biting or chewing. However, your dentist will carefully adjust the bonding material to ensure proper bite alignment. Most patients adapt quickly to the restored tooth contours within a few days.

mainEntity.name: How can I prevent damage to bonded teeth from grinding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wearing a custom night guard consistently provides the best protection against grinding damage. Avoiding hard foods, managing stress, and maintaining regular dental check-ups also help preserve both bonding work and natural tooth structure.

mainEntity.name: Does composite bonding require special care after treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bonded teeth benefit from excellent oral hygiene, including regular brushing with fluoride toothpaste and daily flossing. Avoiding staining substances like coffee or tobacco and using a night guard help maintain both appearance and longevity of the restoration.
